text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels said yesterday the ACCC would examine the pay TV alliance between Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Rupert Murdoch's Foxtel. The combination of Packer interests with Murdoch's considerable programing rights may present an obstacle to a merger between Foxtel and Australis as it would affect competition in the industry. Page 1.

Australian golfer Greg Norman has agreed to a joint venture with the Macquarie Bank to construct golf resorts around the world. Australia will see the first part of the venture, with about five projects proposed for the eastern states, including a course to be opened in Sydney by 2000. Page 1.

Stockmarket researchers predict this reporting season's profit results will be flat compared with last year, but Merrill Lynch's John Banos says he expects resource stocks to outperform industrial stocks. Analysts say lower yields on the bond market and expectations for better conditions will help the market ride out the disappointing conditions. Page 19.

Burns, Philp and Co Ltd chairman Alan McGregor said he was not aware of any influence new major shareholder Graeme Hart had on company management. McGregor said Hart had no role in the appointment of new chief executive Tom Degnan nor the decision a week ago to reach a A$116 million settlement with the trustees of the former Estate Mortgage trusts. Page 19.

ICI Australia managing director Philip Weickhardt said yesterday the company would consider asking shareholders for the funding to buy into a North-West Shelf petrochemical project but indicated the company would almost certainly join with others forsuch a venture, and seek government assistance. Page 20.

Societe Generale Australia's head of securitisation Greg Medcraft has bought a A$3.5 billion portfolio of home loans, government bonds and other assets. Of these assets, A$2 billion worth are Australian, including mortgage-backed bonds which finance Aussie Home Loans (AHL) and other mortgage managers. Medcraft is recognised as an important part of AHL's successful challenge to the banks' mortgage industry. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels said yesterday that access to programming would determine whether the proposal for a Foxtel-Australis merger was approved. Fels said circumstances had changed since an earlier merger proposal was rejected in January last year but the ACCC would have to investigate whether all problems had gone away. Page 17.

Baker and McKenzie law partner Ralph Pliner told a Brisbane mining law conference yesterday Australia's mining and tax laws need an urgent overhaul to improve the gold industry's access to sources of finance following the collapse of the gold price. Pliner warned that unless the gold price rose again many smaller miners and explorers would be forced out of business. Page 17.

St Barbara Mines director and chairman Ross Atkins said at the weekend an agreement with Normandy Mining over the Cuddingwarra gold project in Western Australia is now in dispute because Atkins does not think it is beneficial for his company. The dispute could lead to court proceedings. Page 17.

ICI Australia chief executive Philip Weickhardt said yesterday an aggressive strategy for growth would see the company double in size over the next 10 years. Weickhardt said ICIA would spend up to A$200 million a year on the expansion programme which could include a greenfields chemical joint venture linked to the North-West Shelf. Page 17.

The Association of Mining and Exploration Companies will present Federal Resources Minister Warwick Parer with a submission outlining the major problems of the gold mining industry this morning, with gold producers set to meet with Parer this afternoon. The major problems of the sector include the Reserve Bank's gold reserve sell-off, the diesel fuel rebate, and Western Australia's gold royalty. Page 17.

TNT Australia's Dutch parent, KPN, has approved a management buyout for one of its non-core Australian businesses acquired in last year's A$2 billion takeover. TNT chief executive David Mortimer, who will head TNT's Australian and Asian operations under KPN's restructuring, said only that the asset was "one of our smaller divisions". Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Stockbroking strategists and fund managers say a weak Australian economy will lead to inconsistent and lacklustre results in the annual profit season. The industrial company sector overall is expected to show a negative return in earnings of up to five percent, and resource stocks may fall back or just break even. Page 37.

Last week's decision by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission to allow Westpac's bid for the Bank of Melbourne to go ahead has led to the prospect of more corporate plays in the banking sector, with Bank of Queensland , Adelaide Bank and Colonial all shaping up as prime candidates. Page 37.

Optus Communications chief executive officer Peter Howell-Davies said yesterday the merger between Foxtel and Australis Media looks to be going ahead simply for Telstra's benefit and could potentially reinforce Telstra's local call dominance. Howell-Daves has vowed to derail the proposed merger. Page 37.

The Diggers and Dealers conference in Kalgoorlie on Tuesday will hear from West Australian Premier Richard Court who is expected to unveil the revised gold royalty package. Court said negotiations with the gold industry were continuing, and the new deal would involve deferring the dates on which the two-phase royalty was introduced. Page 39.

Employees of the Commonwealth Bank will hold a stop-work meeting today as part of a campaign against massive restructuring and a lack of consultation with workers. The meeting signals the start of a battle between unions and the big banks, with CBA and the National Australia Bank already negotiating enterprise agreements. Page 39.

Qantas Airways has enjoyed an increase in its share price to A$3.12, only thre cents off its all time high, with a positive earnings outlook from analysts boosting the share performance. The release of its monthly traffic report for May showed an increase international business of 11.3 percent over the same month last year. Page 39.
THE AGE

United States-based Atlantic International Entertainment, which is planning to join the Australian Stock Exchange this year, is expected to announce an Australian telecommunications joint venture this week. The Internet gambling company is bringing in business seen as both a threat and a potential market by the large casinos. Page B1.

Following a meeting with Normandy Mining executives last Friday, St Barbara Mining executive chairman Ross Atkins said yesterday the company would be backing out of its month-old deal with Normandy to mine Western Australia's Big Bell-Cuddingwarra gold jont venture. Page B1.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Professor Allan Fels told yesterday's Business Sunday program that the regulator would view the proposed merger between Foxtel and Australis more favourably due to changes in Australia's pay-TV industry since the last proposal. Page B1.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics has reported that the turnaround in Australia's trade of services since 1991 is the result of increased exports of Australia's tourism and education services. Australia's trade surplus in educational services jumped by A$1,53 billion and the surplus on tourism spending rose by A$1.73 billion. Page B3.

The Leading Edge Group, which consists of 630 shops from diverse retail sectors, is designed to reduce costs and provide stronger buying and marketing potential to its members. Networks such as this have developed because of a drop in sales due to change in spending by Australian consumers. Page B2.

DDI Asia Pacific, a human resource consultancy, has conducted a study of over 100 small business operators which found that between A$2,000 and A$20,000 is lost each year through the costs associated with poor employment policies such as low morale, absenteeism, staff turnover and reduced output. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
